newsitem.title: GERMANY: Helaba buys 50 pct of German leasing firm.
newsitem.headline: Helaba buys 50 pct of German leasing firm.

text.p: Landesbank Hessen-Thueringen (Helaba) said on Thursday it had bought a 50 percent stake in Hannover Leasing GmbH & Co KG, a major German leasing company.
The stake was bought on October 31, Helaba said in a statement. It did not disclose the purchase price.
Helaba said IVG Holding had bought a 25 percent stake in Hannover Leasing.
Helaba said Hannover Leasing's business has a volume of about 6.2 billion marks and covers aircraft, industrial plant, real estate and vehicles.
The bank said the stake purchase was aimed at broadening its product range in the field of fund-based and special financing, particularly on behalf of the public sector and large corporate clients.
Helaba acts as central clearing institution for the savings banks in the states of Hesse and Thuringia.

Helaba said it and Hannover Leasing had already cooperated before the stake purchase. Together they had provided financing for power stations, real estate and aircraft worth almost two billion marks, Helaba said.

Apart from the 25 percent stake in Hannover Leasing bought by state-owned holding company IVG Holding, 20 percent is owned by the company's management and five percent by two other shareholders, Helaba said.
